_why: NOT A CAPTURE RECORD — A COPY RECORD, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT. The android-play
CAPTURE.json says which BUILD was photographed. This file cannot say that, because nothing
photographed anything for this channel: these four PNGs are byte-identical copies of the Play
phone set. So it records the copy instead — source path, SHA-256, and the posture of the run
that produced the original — and deliberately does NOT claim `capturedBy`, which would assert
that tooling/store/capture-play-screenshots.mjs wrote into this directory. It did not.
WHY A COPY IS LEGITIMATE HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE IN THIS TREE: this channel distributes the
SAME .apk the android-play lane produces. Same build, same platform, same four screens. The
desktop channels forbid borrowing because they ship different builds; that reason does not
THE HASHES ARE THE MECHANISM. If android-play's set is re-captured and this one is not, the
sha256 values below stop matching the files they name, and `copiedFrom` names exactly where to
look. A copy that has quietly stopped being one is the failure this file exists to make visible.
_postureWhy: Inherited from the source set's CAPTURE.json, not re-measured. The Play phone set was captured against a LIVE build — not a demo build, whose every screen carries a "Demo data" banner and whose board is twelve third-party trademarks. A demo capture may not be copied here either.

requirements._why: THE STORE PUBLISHES NO ASSET SPECIFICATION AT ALL. The NeGD App Hosting & Security Guidelines PDF (18 pages, read in full 2026-09-20) mentions listing media exactly once, in §4.1: "Listing Confirmation: Developers verify store details (screenshots, feature graphic, T&C)." No pixels, no counts, no formats, no caps. The real spec, if one exists, is behind the authenticated SPA at apps.gov.in/Developer, which agents never log in to. NOT SPECIFIED is the measured answer; an invented limit fires on correct input.
